evidence.note: Established a baseline (i32.json 2/459) before making changes, so improvement could be measured against a known starting point.

After implementation ran individual per-family jsons (i32, block, simd_const, call_indirect, memory) and built /tmp/runall.sh aggregate runner; caught that call_indirect/memory crashed (empty output) via per-file inspection.

Repeatedly categorized FAIL lines by assertion type (grep 'FAIL: assert_return/trap/malformed'), isolating the handful of functional failures apart from the mass of assert_invalid, then drilled each to its exact test file/line.

Diagnosed genuine semantic edge cases from individual FAIL lines: trunc saturation boundary (-2147483648.9), and f32.nearest tie-to-even producing -0.0 vs -2.0 — reading expected vs got bit patterns per assertion.
Distinguished an encoding/semantic bug from expectation: load8_splat reading 2 bytes ([0,1] pattern) vs 1, traced to decode/exec rather than assuming test wrong.

When adding the validator, monitored the aggregate and caught MVP regressions ('no current module', block.0.wasm valid module rejected), fixed pop_ctrl before proceeding — guarding MVP while adding validation.

Treated the aggregate pass rate as a monitored signal (95.4%→99.4%→99.8%→99.91%→100%), pursuing exact 1.0 rather than 'mostly passing', then re-ran the suggested per-family commands and the runner to confirm 34212/34212.

reasoning: The agent's verification is engineered and self-correcting: it drilled into individual failing assertions to diagnose semantic edge cases (nearest tie-to-even, trunc boundary, sign/-0.0), distinguished real bugs from encoding mismatches (load_splat), guarded against MVP regressions when integrating the validator, and treated the aggregate score as a continuously monitored signal driving toward an exact 1.0 — matching the level-10 description. It falls just short of a pure 10 because the entire SIMD surface was written in one monolithic batch before any test ran, rather than an implement→run-family-json→fix loop per family during construction; the systematic per-family/per-assertion discipline appears mainly in the debugging phase afterward.
